search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; reusable-validation selection correction; nonuniform transcript priors; prefix/mixture coding; fresh-audit switching; prior misspecification robustness

public_sources.title: What Fits (Into Few Tokens) Doesn't Overfit: Compression and Generalization in ML Research Agents
public_sources.authors: Martin Andres Bertran; Aaron Roth; Zhiwei Steven Wu
public_sources.used_scope: Agentic input compression via one-bit ladder. The validation-dependent view is the binary improve/not-improve transcript; the j-th improvement checkpoint has a finite transcript class determined by improvement locations. The paper explicitly notes uniform token/transcript bounds can be loose and suggests sharper prior-weighted/PAC-Bayes descriptions as an open direction.

public_sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
public_sources.authors: Cynthia Dwork; Vitaly Feldman; Moritz Hardt; Toniann Pitassi; Omer Reingold; Aaron Roth
public_sources.used_scope: Description-length control for adaptive reuse: if prior outputs expose k bits, a union bound inflates a fixed-analysis failure probability by at most 2^k. Also motivates separating data-independent decoder/prior design from validation-dependent selection.

public_sources.title: A unified recipe for deriving (time-uniform) PAC-Bayes bounds
public_sources.authors: Ben Chugg; Hongjian Wang; Aaditya Ramdas
public_sources.used_scope: Time-uniform PAC-Bayes construction from nonnegative supermartingales, mixtures, convex duality and Ville. Used as support for prior-weighted time-uniform complexity accounting; not used as a direct theorem for the worker-local selected-candidate e-process rule.

public_sources.title: Minimum Description Length Revisited
public_sources.used_scope: MDL perspective that nonuniform code/probability assignments can replace flat model counting, with complexity determined by code/probability mass rather than raw class cardinality.

public_sources.title: On the role of data in PAC-Bayes bounds
public_sources.authors: Gintare Karolina Dziugaite; Kyle Hsu; Waseem Gharbieh; Gabriel Arpino; Daniel M. Roy
public_sources.used_scope: Data-dependent priors can tighten certificates only when their data use is structurally separated from the empirical-risk term; used as a scope warning that fitting transcript priors on the same reused validation channel requires an additional validity argument or split, not as a direct e-process theorem.

hierarchical_transcript_prior.setup: For a validation-dependent transcript u, factor prior mass as pi(u)=pi_core(stop_time, feedback_pattern)*pi_family(f)*pi_metadata(m), with every factor fixed before observing the reused validation data. The weighted-anytime commit threshold from the previous checkpoint becomes E_u >= 1/(alpha*pi(u)).

components.name: flat_fallback
components.feedback: iid Bernoulli(0.5) over the realized pre-stop bits

core_mixture.exact_pattern_mass: For structured component (s,h), pi(t,bits)=P_capped_geom_s(t)*h^r*(1-h)^(t-1-r), where r is the number of improvement bits among the t-1 feedback bits. The flat fallback assigns (1/50)*2^{-(t-1)}.
core_mixture.robust_regret_bound_bits: Because each of the four components has weight 1/4, -log2(pi_core(u)) <= -log2(pi_c(u))+2 for every transcript u and every component c. In particular, prior misspecification can cost at most 2 bits relative to the flat fallback, while retaining large gains on sparse/early-stop transcripts.

hierarchical_transcript_prior.candidate_family_prior: If candidate families are assigned a validation-independent canonical integer index k>=1, use pi_family(k)=1/[k(k+1)]. This telescopes to one and charges log2(k(k+1)) bits. A learned/custom family prior is allowed only if trained independently of the reused validation channel or its own selection cost is separately paid.
hierarchical_transcript_prior.metadata_prior: For a validation-dependent metadata bitstring m of length ell>=0, use pi_L(ell)=1/[(ell+1)(ell+2)] and pi_metadata(m)=pi_L(ell)*2^{-ell}. This charges ell + log2((ell+1)(ell+2)) bits and prevents hidden stop-time/metadata side channels from being treated as free.
hierarchical_transcript_prior.scope_guard: These are worker-local prior constructions. The numerical component parameters are illustrative, validation-independent codebook candidates, not empirical claims about any deployed system. Any parameter tuning using the same reused validation transcript must itself be indexed/charged or done on separate data.

flat_fallback_mixture_guard.mechanism: Always reserve nonzero prior mass for a broad flat transcript component. Then a structured prior cannot catastrophically invalidate or arbitrarily over-penalize an unforeseen transcript: with fallback weight w0, its code is at most -log2(w0) bits worse than flat for every path.
flat_fallback_mixture_guard.four_component_special_case: With w0=0.25 the worst-case excess relative to flat is <=2 bits. The same <=2-bit regret holds relative to each structured component because all four weights are equal.
flat_fallback_mixture_guard.measurement_value: Prior design can be optimized for expected power without turning prior misspecification into an unbounded certificate penalty. This is a stronger operational requirement than reporting average code length alone.

fresh_audit_switch_rule.setup: Under the prior checkpoint's stylized paired-sign alternative q=0.75, discordance rate rho=0.4 and fixed bet 0.75, expected log-e growth per independent task is g=rho*KL(Bern(q)||Bern(0.5))=0.0523248144 nats/task.
fresh_audit_switch_rule.selection_bit_exchange_rate: Each additional selection-complexity bit raises the log threshold by ln 2, costing approximately ln(2)/g = 13.247 independent task-equivalents in expected log-growth.
fresh_audit_switch_rule.base_alpha_0_05: The unpenalized expected-log threshold ln(20)/g is about 57.253 tasks.
fresh_audit_switch_rule.hybrid_rule: If a fresh confirmation block of A independent tasks is available, paying a transcript penalty B bits is expected-log more expensive than that block once B > A*g/ln2. Under this stylized alternative the break-even is about 1.51 bits for A=20, 3.77 bits for A=50, and 7.55 bits for A=100.
fresh_audit_switch_rule.scope_guard: This is an expected-log heuristic, not an exact finite-sample power theorem. Actual stopping power depends on discreteness, bet choice, effect size, discordance and task distribution.

prior_learning_boundary.rule: A nonuniform prior is selection-safe only to the extent its probability assignment is fixed independently of the reused validation information whose adaptivity it is correcting. Hyperparameter/codebook selection from training-only data, simulation, public data or a disjoint prior-building split is admissible in principle; tuning it on the same validation transcript requires another selection-cost layer, a stability/privacy theorem, or a fresh split.
prior_learning_boundary.reason: Otherwise prior learning itself becomes a validation-dependent side channel and the claimed code length understates the counterfactual selection universe.
prior_learning_boundary.scope_guard: The analogy to data-dependent PAC-Bayes priors is conceptual; a direct theorem for this exact weighted-e construction would need to be stated separately.

exact_expected_core_code_bits.method: Exact summation over stop time t=1..50 and improvement count r, weighting all exact bit patterns under each stylized true regime. Family/metadata costs excluded so the table isolates one-bit-ladder transcript cost.
exact_expected_core_code_bits.interpretation: The flat fallback keeps the mixture close to flat even outside the intended sparse/early-stop regimes, while the structured mixture saves roughly 4-8 bits in the three represented regimes. Under the stylized q=.75,rho=.4 evidence rate those savings correspond to about 54,82,104 task-equivalents of expected log-threshold respectively.
exact_expected_core_code_bits.scope_guard: The regimes are worker-local stress-test distributions, not observed frequencies in any external system.

power_stress_test.simulation: 100000 independent Monte Carlo evidence trajectories per regime/prior, seed 20260826. Selection code B was sampled from the corresponding stylized transcript regime. After candidate selection, an independent paired-sign evidence process used rho=.4, q=.75, factor 1.5 on candidate-only win, 0.5 on incumbent-only win, 1 on concordance, alpha=.05, threshold 20*2^B. This isolates threshold-cost effects; it is not a simulation of the full adaptive proposal loop.
power_stress_test.interpretation: A nonuniform robust prior can materially recover finite-horizon power versus flat transcript counting, but even the improved 6-23 bit penalties remain expensive at 10-50 task horizons. This strengthens the case for a hybrid switch to fresh confirmation rather than insisting on reused-validation certification for every transcript.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Use a predeclared mixture over plausible stop/improvement transcript models plus a flat fallback, then charge the realized transcript by -log2 mixture mass in the weighted-anytime certificate.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local exact code calculations and 100k-trajectory finite-horizon stress tests; grounded in description-length adaptive-data analysis and time-uniform mixture/PAC-Bayes principles.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Mixture components and weights must be validation-independent or their selection cost must be paid. Numeric parameters are illustrative stress-test codebooks.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Reserve explicit prior weight for a flat transcript model. With weight 1/4, the structured mixture is never more than 2 bits worse than flat on any transcript and never more than 2 bits worse than any one equal-weight component.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct mixture-probability inequality; no stochastic assumptions required beyond the predeclared probability assignment.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: This bounds certificate complexity regret, not statistical power regret under every effect distribution.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Compute realized transcript complexity before confirmation and switch to fresh audit when the selection-bit penalty is larger than the expected evidence carried by an available fresh block, instead of mechanically paying the reused-data penalty.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local expected-log calculation plus prior simulation showing 6-23 bit penalties remain severe at short horizons even after nonuniform coding.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Switch threshold must be calibrated to the actual evidence process/effect regime; the reported 13.247 tasks per bit is only for q=.75,rho=.4,fixed-bet=.75.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Treat transcript-prior construction itself as part of the evaluation protocol: learn/tune it only from validation-independent information, or explicitly charge/meta-correct its data dependence.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Adaptive-data description-length logic plus PAC-Bayes data-dependent-prior literature showing prior/data separation is a first-class validity concern.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Direct selected-e theorem for data-dependent priors remains to be derived; use this as a safety gate, not a claimed equivalence to PAC-Bayes.

measurement_validity_rules.rule_1: Report realized selection complexity as -log2 prior mass, not only raw feedback bit count. Sparse/early-stop transcripts can be much cheaper than flat worst-case counting, but only under a predeclared probability assignment.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_2: Always include a broad fallback component in a power-optimized transcript prior and report worst-case regret to that fallback, not just average code length.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_3: Candidate-family choice, stop time and metadata are free only if genuinely validation-independent or mechanically hidden; otherwise they are part of the adaptive transcript and must receive prior mass.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_4: Do not tune the transcript prior on the same reused validation interactions and then evaluate complexity under that tuned prior without an additional selection correction.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_5: At short task horizons, compare transcript-corrected reuse against fresh confirmation on the same utility axis. A formally valid reused-data certificate can be practically dominated by fresh audit when its code penalty is several bits.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_6: Mixture-prior robustness should be expressed pathwise: pi_mix>=w_c*pi_c implies at most -log2 w_c extra bits for every transcript, independent of whether the deployment distribution matches the component.

rejected_overgeneralizations: Uniform transcript counting is the only selection-safe description-length correction.
A nonuniform prior learned after seeing the reused validation transcript is automatically valid because its final probabilities sum to one.
A prior that has lower average code length is necessarily safer; without a fallback it can impose arbitrarily bad penalties on misspecified paths.

Saving several description bits makes reused-validation certification automatically preferable to fresh audit; at small task horizons one bit can represent more than ten task-equivalents of expected log evidence in the tested stylized regime.

Candidate family and metadata can be ignored because the visible validation response is only one bit per query; any validation-dependent side channel that changes the selected candidate belongs in the transcript complexity.

frontier_queue.action: Derive an empirical-Bayes-like but validation-safe way to adapt mixture weights from prior runs or disjoint prior-building data, with explicit accounting when source runs are correlated. Compare static equal-weight mixture, hierarchical universal prior and split-learned prior.

Build a full adaptive proposal-loop simulator where the same validation transcript generates the next candidate, then compare naive reused PACE, flat prefix-weighted replay, robust mix4 replay and fresh-audit switching on false commits, power, total task usage and information returned to the proposer.

Replace the stylized Bernoulli improvement-hazard codebook with a validation-independent context-tree or finite-state transcript model and verify a pathwise regret bound against the flat fallback. Determine whether the extra model flexibility saves enough bits to offset mixture overhead.

Derive a direct theorem for data-dependent transcript priors in the weighted-anytime selected-e setting, separating safe split priors, DP/stability-limited priors and priors whose own selection must be charged.

Quantify the hybrid switch frontier under q in {0.60,0.65,0.70,0.75,0.80}, discordance in {0.2,0.4,0.6}, and fresh-block sizes 20-200, reporting resolved rate and unresolved rate rather than expected-log cost alone.

exact_next_action: Construct a full adaptive proposal-loop simulator with validation-dependent candidate generation and a predeclared robust transcript mixture prior, then compare flat weighting, mix4 weighting and fresh-audit switching under both null and alternative across 10-200 independent tasks; separately derive how mixture weights may be learned from disjoint prior-building data without contaminating the reused validation certificate.
